prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A weekly class timetable for quick lookup of when a lesson occurs, what subject it is, who teaches it, where it meets, and any notes.","reading":"Read right-to-left: scan the merged day blocks first, then the time within each day, then read across subject → teacher → room; notes are secondary and consulted only after the lesson row is identified.","groups":["Columns 1–2 (day + time) form the schedule anchor and should stay adjacent and dominant.","Columns 3–5 (subject + teacher + room) form the lesson identity and should read as a compact row unit.","Column 6 (notes) is ancillary and should not compete with the schedule or lesson columns."],"keep_intact":["Day names","Time ranges, ideally unbroken","Subject names without mid-word splits","Teacher names, allowing wraps between words","Room identifiers where possible"],"may_wrap":["Notes text, freely","Teacher names between words","Long subject words only when forced","Room labels only when forced"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[62,82,64,52,44,55],"idea":"No-scroll compact layout: preserve day and give time priority, then squeeze the lesson columns and let notes wrap into a narrow trailing column."},{"name":"B","widths":[62,110,84,89,97,100],"idea":"Key-column integrity: keep day, time, subject, teacher and room at one-line widths and accept horizontal scrolling mainly for a moderately narrow notes column."},{"name":"C","widths":[62,110,95,85,80,180],"idea":"Notes-readable wide layout: keep schedule anchors and subject intact, allow teacher/room to wrap at word boundaries, and give notes enough width to remain useful while scrolling."}]}
